Mechanical Engineer positions available in all states NSW, Qld, Vic, & WA

At NEPEAN™ we are proud to be Australia’s leading privately owned engineering, mining services and industrial manufacturing organisation. We have unique capabilities to deliver high value, innovative and sustainable solutions for the world’s leading mining, construction, and transport companies. Over the last 40 years, hard work, technical credibility, and a willingness to tackle very difficult projects have earned NEPEAN an enviable reputation. Today our organisation employs over 1400 people across six continents and distributes products to more than 65 countries.

We service our customers through multiple businesses in our portfolio: NEPEAN Building and Infrastructure (Galserv, Galintel, Weldlok), NEPEAN Engineering and Innovation, NEPEAN Power, Mining (NEPEAN Longwall), PROK, NEPEAN Conveyors, NEPEAN Transport, Gurtec, Roxon, and NEPEAN Belting Mackay.

We are currently offering a fantastic opportunity for Mechanical Engineer based in our WA Office. The Mechanical Engineer will attend various customer’s mine sites and assist our valued customers with conveyor systems providing solutions to engineering-related problems. Critical to the role is the employee can develop and nurture professional, productive and harmonious working relationships with the ongoing goal of customer satisfaction, loyalty and trust.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES

ENGINEERING
Applying sound Mechanical Engineering practices to the safe design of conveyor equipment
Applying structural engineering practices to the safe design of conveyor equipment, including winch design and structures
Analysing inputs and outputs from many in-house design calculators and spreadsheets, written to ensure output is conforming to relevant Australian Standards
Conduct finite Element Analysis and Element Modelling using Inventor, ANSYS and Rocky
Conduct Power and tension calculations and reports for conveyor systems
Understanding the installation, operation and maintenance of industrial equipment, especially conveyors
Develop operation parts and maintenance manuals as well as commissioning documentation, SOP’s, design reviews, risk assessments etc

MODELLING AND DRAFTING
Conduct 3D modelling in Inventor to develop conveyor equipment concepts to a point that they can be detailed by the drafting team
Occasional detail drafting as required

SALES
Development and nurturing of existing PROK-client relationships
Developing new relationships with new client representatives and/or new clients
Being the primary site-based point of contact for all correspondence between the client and PROK
Develop scopes of work with the client and provide pricing sketches and work with the estimators to ensure sufficient information is communicated

PLANNING
Maintain and update a personal engineering planning sheet with your allocated clients and projects every week
Monitor and control the schedule, budget and quality of each assigned work/drawing package

TECHNICAL WRITING
Prepare clear, grammatically correct, professional operation, parts and maintenance manuals with input from engineering team, workshop, client and suppliers
Develop commissioning documentation
Participate/ develop/ complete SOPs and similar tasks

EDUCATION, QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE
Mechanical Engineering Degree and/or Structural Engineering Degree
On-site and commissioning experience desirable

SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE
Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills
Be well organised, extremely personable and reliable. (Hands-on skills)
The ability to strategically evaluate and solve complex problems
Strong attention to detail
Adaptability and Flexibility
An understanding of organisational development
Work personality strongly aligns with NEPEAN’s DNA
Mechanical Engineering Practices
Team Player
Conflict Resolution

If you believe you the right skills, experience and passion for succeeding in this role, please submit your cover letter and resume for consideration.

NEPEAN believes in diversity and is committed to providing Equal Employment opportunities for all applicants. We welcome applicants from all walks of life which also included various socio-economic, cultural, LGBTIQ, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander backgrounds.

Salary: $85,000 per annum + Super

Custom Clad is a specialist façade and cladding subcontractor delivering architectural building envelope solutions across commercial, residential and institutional projects. We are seeking a full-time Structural Engineer (ANZSCO 233214) to join our engineering team.

Key tasks and duties

Determine the structural design methods and materials to be used in façade, cladding and framing systems, and provide specifications for their construction.
Prepare and interpret engineering sketches, drawings, plans and specifications for building envelope elements and support structures.
Analyse and assess the behaviour of structural systems and components under load, including wind, dead and live loading, to ensure structural integrity and compliance with the National Construction Code and relevant Australian Standards.
Perform structural calculations and design checks for cladding substrates, subframes, brackets and fixings, and provide certification input where required.
Provide technical advice on structural and engineering matters to project managers, estimators, site teams and clients.
Coordinate with architects, builders, building surveyors and consultants to resolve design and buildability issues.
Conduct site inspections and investigate structural failures or defects, and prepare reports on findings and remedial recommendations.
Organise and direct site labour and delivery of materials, plant and equipment in relation to engineered structural elements.
Ensure engineering work complies with Australian Standards, workplace health and safety requirements and quality assurance procedures.
Skills and experience

Bachelor or Master degree in Structural or Civil Engineering (AQF Level 7 or higher).
Positive skills assessment from Engineers Australia (or eligibility to obtain one).
Sound knowledge of the National Construction Code and relevant Australian Standards, including AS/NZS 1170 and AS 4100.
Proficiency in structural analysis and design software and AutoCAD or Revit.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary project team.
How to apply

Submit your CV and a brief cover letter outlining your relevant qualifications and experience.

Job Type: Full-time
Salary: A$79,500.00 - A$95,000.00 per year
Work Location: In person

We are looking for a skilled and motivated Chemical Engineer to join our team and contribute to the design, development, and optimisation of chemical process systems and commercial-scale plant operations. The successful candidate will apply their technical expertise to ensure safe, efficient, and compliant processing of materials undergoing physical and chemical changes. This role suits an analytical and solutions-focused professional with a strong foundation in chemical engineering principles and a commitment to continuous improvement. You will play a key role in driving operational excellence while upholding the highest standards of safety and environmental responsibility.

## Key Responsibilities

- Design and develop detailed specifications for chemical process systems, including separation, heat transfer, reaction, and fluid handling operations, ensuring all designs meet engineering standards and project requirements
- Plan, implement, and oversee control systems for a range of chemical processes, including the storage and handling of solids, liquids, and gases
- Monitor the day-to-day operation and maintenance of plant equipment to maximise efficiency, minimise downtime, and ensure safe operating conditions are maintained at all times
- Diagnose technical malfunctions and process inefficiencies within chemical plant systems, and lead the implementation of remedial and corrective actions
- Verify that all materials, components, and equipment conform to relevant technical specifications, industry standards, and regulatory requirements
- Evaluate and improve product utilisation strategies, identifying opportunities to reduce waste, increase yield, and enhance overall process performance
- Lead and contribute to pollution control initiatives, assessing environmental impact and implementing sustainable engineering solutions in line with applicable legislation
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams including operations, maintenance, safety, and procurement to support the successful delivery of projects and plant improvements
- Conduct process modelling, simulation, and analysis to support design decisions, troubleshooting efforts, and capacity planning activities
- Prepare and review technical documentation including engineering reports, process flow diagrams, equipment specifications, and operating procedures
- Ensure all engineering activities are carried out in accordance with workplace health and safety (WHS) obligations and site-specific safety management systems
- Support the commissioning, testing, and validation of new or modified plant equipment and process systems

## Required Qualifications & Skills

- Bachelor's degree or higher in Chemical Engineering or a closely related discipline from a recognised Australian or overseas institution
- Eligibility for membership with Engineers Australia (EA), or current membership highly regarded
- Demonstrated experience in the design and operation of chemical process systems within an industrial or manufacturing environment
- Strong working knowledge of process control, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, mass transfer, and reaction engineering
- Proficiency in engineering design and simulation tools such as Aspen HYSYS, MATLAB, or equivalent process modelling software
- Sound understanding of Australian and relevant international standards, codes of practice, and regulatory frameworks applicable to chemical plant operations
- Proven ability to diagnose complex plant malfunctions and develop practical, evidence-based solutions in a timely manner
- Solid understanding of workplace health and safety legislation, hazardous materials management, and risk assessment methodologies including HAZOP
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a meticulous attention to detail
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to prepare clear technical documentation and liaise effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders
- Ability to manage competing priorities and deliver outcomes within project timelines and budget constraints

## Preferred Qualifications

- Postgraduate qualifications in Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, or a related field
- Chartered Professional Engineer (CPEng) status with Engineers Australia
- Experience with pollution control systems, environmental compliance monitoring, or sustainability-focused process improvement
- Familiarity with lean manufacturing principles, Six Sigma methodologies, or continuous improvement frameworks
- Experience working within regulated industries such as oil and gas, mining and minerals processing, pharmaceuticals, food and beverage, or water treatment
- Knowledge of functional safety standards and safety instrumented systems (SIS)
- Previous experience in project engineering or a lead engineering capacity

## Why Join Us?

- Be part of a collaborative and forward-thinking engineering team that values innovation, technical excellence, and professional growth
- Access ongoing learning and development opportunities, including support for further study, professional memberships, and industry conference attendance
- Enjoy a flexible and supportive work environment that promotes work-life balance and employee wellbeing
- Contribute to meaningful projects that have a tangible impact on sustainability, safety, and industrial efficiency across Australia
- Competitive remuneration package with opportunities for career progression within a growing organisation

## Job Details

- Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
- Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Superannuation
